subagent_reports.topic: Phase 9 archive timeout override + durable pre-finalization checkpoint (GH #216)

sources.label: safeExecute timeout override mechanism
sources.summary: DEFAULT_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS=10_000 (L240). SafeExecuteOptions.timeoutMs override (L247-250). raceWithTimeout uses Promise.race against a setTimeout that rejects with ToolExecutionTimeoutError (L275-289). On timeout the outer Promise.race rejects the whole tool promise — the wrapped fn keeps running but its own try/catch never surfaces because the race already rejected. safeExecute reads timeoutMs=options?.timeoutMs ?? DEFAULT (L433).

sources.label: Existing per-tool override registrations (exact seam)
sources.summary: Named-override pattern: registerTool(desc,args,namedExecute(name, safeExecute(execFn, name, undefined, { timeoutMs: N }))). adv_run_test=305_000, adv_task_checkpoint=35_000, adv_temporal_worker_restart=15_000. Each carries an inline rationale comment; worker_restart cites rq-toolTimeoutOverride01.2.

sources.label: adv_change_archive currently has NO override (root cause)
sources.summary: adv_change_archive is registered via plain bindTool(changeTools.adv_change_archive, "adv_change_archive", store). bindTool (L215-228) calls safeExecute(fn, name) with no options → inherits the 10s default ceiling. This is the direct cause of GH #216: Phase 9 git+Temporal work exceeds 10s, race rejects, tool-local failed-status catch is bypassed.

sources.label: Override test seam (structural registry guard)
sources.summary: describe('safeExecute timeout overrides for slow-subprocess tools') reads tool-registry.ts as source text, extractRegistrationBlock(src,toolName) walks balanced parens from '<name>: registerTool(', asserts /timeoutMs:\s*(\d[\d_]*)/ >= threshold. NOTE: extractor anchors on 'registerTool(' — a bindTool-registered tool is NOT matched. Adding an archive override requires converting adv_change_archive from bindTool to an explicit registerTool block (like adv_gate_complete L714-728) so the guard can assert it.

sources.label: Phase9 finalization flow — no pre-finalization checkpoint
sources.summary: finalizeRelease/verifyReleaseEvidenceFromMain is awaited at L2692-2706 inside try. recordPhase9Status is only ever called AFTER the await resolves: failed in catch (L2711), pending_merge (L2758), done (L2862). There is NO recordPhase9Status BEFORE L2692. A 10s outer-race rejection kills the promise before the catch runs → zero durable phase9_status is written → split-brain (bundle written by archiveChange at L2660, terminal status absent).

sources.label: Phase9FinalizationStatusSchema enum (widening target)
sources.summary: status enum is ["pending","pending_merge","done","failed"] with startedAt(required), completedAt/error/route/changeTipSha optional. No in_progress/started member exists to mark 'finalization dispatched, not yet terminal'.

sources.label: Workflow signal handler is opaque assignment (replay-safe widening)
sources.summary: phase9StatusUpdatedSignal handler does state.phase9_status = payload.phase9_status — no exhaustive switch on the enum in workflow-reachable code. Seed (L628) and projection (L1715) also opaque. recordPhase9Status fires phase9StatusUpdatedSignal via fireSignalAndRefresh. Adding an enum member introduces no new signal/handler/branch → replay-safe; only the Zod boundary widens.

sources.label: Existing bundle-present retry / reconciliation seams
sources.summary: findArchiveBundle probes existing bundle (L2567). rq-archiveRetryIdempotence01: if status==archived && bundle present → reconcileArchivedBundleRetry (bounded metadata-only, L2610-2625). rq-archiveOrdering01: if bundle present but status!=archived → synthetic archiveResult, skip disk re-write, let status transition complete recovery (L2636-2658). reconcileArchivedBundleRetry (archive-gate.ts:290-431) re-verifies structural release proof + durable proof before no-op success.

sources.label: Relevant spec requirements
sources.summary: rq-releaseFinalization01 (finalization→gate ordering, shipped invariant, .1-.12), rq-releaseProjectionDurability01 (durable proof or block), rq-archiveRecoveryConsistency01 (failed recovery must classify + fail closed), rq-archiveOrdering01 (resilient to failed disk write), rq-archiveRetryIdempotence01 (bounded reconcile). A new AC for pre-finalization durable checkpoint fits under rq-releaseFinalization01 or a sibling rq-releaseFinalization01.N.

sources.label: Failed-status regression test seam (proven harness)
sources.summary: mocks.finalizeRelease.mockRejectedValueOnce(...) then asserts mocks.workflow.signalPayloads containsEqual phase9_status.status='failed' and store.changes.save NOT called. Same mock harness (createMockStore, mocks.workflow.signalPayloads) can assert an 'in_progress'/'started' payload is fired BEFORE finalization and that a timeout leaves durable actionable state.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: GH #216 root cause is precise and single-seam: adv_change_archive (tool-registry.ts:379-382) is bound via bindTool with no SafeExecuteOptions, inheriting the 10s DEFAULT_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS. Phase 9 legitimately does cumulative git + Temporal work exceeding 10s; safe-execute.ts raceWithTimeout rejects the tool promise, and because the ONLY durable phase9_status writes (change.ts:2711/2758/2862) occur AFTER the awaited finalization resolves, an outer-timeout abort bypasses all of them — no failed, no pending_merge, no done. Result: archive bundle present (archiveChange ran at L2660) with terminal projection absent = the exact split-brain wedge the change targets. Two mutually-reinforcing fixes: (1) explicit archive timeout override, (2) a durable pre-finalization checkpoint. The retry/reconciliation machinery to consume that checkpoint already exists (reconcileArchivedBundleRetry, rq-archiveOrdering01 synthetic-result recovery, rq-archiveRetryIdempotence01) — the missing durable link is a status set BEFORE the vulnerable await, independent of the inner catch.

validation.notes: The proposed direction is architecturally sound and low-risk. Fix 1 (timeout override) is a mechanical extension of a proven pattern (adv_run_test/adv_task_checkpoint/adv_temporal_worker_restart). Fix 2 (pre-finalization checkpoint) requires: (a) convert adv_change_archive from bindTool to an explicit registerTool block so the timeoutMs override is expressible AND the registry guard test can assert it — bindTool cannot carry SafeExecuteOptions and the extractor only matches 'registerTool('; (b) call recordPhase9Status with a non-terminal 'in_progress'/'started' status immediately before the finalizeRelease/verify await at change.ts:2692; (c) widen Phase9FinalizationStatusSchema enum — replay-safe because the workflow handler is an opaque assignment with no exhaustive switch. Suggested budget: 180s (matches proposal; must exceed archive's cumulative git+Temporal ceiling and stay under the SDK output-race practicalities; note adv_run_test already sets 305s so 180s is well within precedent).

tradeoffs: Converting adv_change_archive from bindTool to registerTool adds ~15 lines of explicit wiring but is required for both the override and its structural guard test; this trades one-line brevity for testability and matches the existing adv_gate_complete precedent (L714-728).

A non-terminal 'in_progress' phase9_status must NOT satisfy any release/shipped invariant check — every existing consumer that treats status!=done as incomplete (change.ts:2858-2861, archive-gate.ts:399-401) already fails-closed, so widening is safe, but any future code that switches on the enum must handle the new member.

An explicit override does not itself fix a genuinely-hung finalization (infinite git prompt); the 180s bound converts an unbounded hang into a bounded failure. The pre-finalization checkpoint is what makes that bounded failure durable and recoverable — both are needed together, not either alone.

The 180s budget is advisory; if archive later grows heavier work it must be re-tuned, and the inner git/Temporal ops remain the authoritative wall-clock source (mirroring the adv_run_test 305s comment at tool-registry.ts:732-738).

alternatives_considered.option: Timeout override alone (raise archive to 180s, no checkpoint)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Reduces incidence but does not eliminate the class: any interruption after bundle write and before the post-await recordPhase9Status (worker loss, process kill, a >180s hang) reproduces the split-brain. The durable invariant requires a checkpoint written BEFORE the vulnerable await, independent of the inner catch (proposal item 2).

Makes the wedge recoverable but leaves the 10s ceiling routinely aborting legitimate finalizations, so every long archive still fails first-try. Poor operator UX and unnecessary retries. Both fixes are complementary.

alternatives_considered.option: Add a defineUpdate handler / detached async workflow to own Phase 9 out-of-band
alternatives_considered.rationale: Violates the project's signal-only change-workflow constraint (AGENTS.md: no defineUpdate in workflow-reachable code) and the 'no general Temporal worker supervision redesign' out-of-scope boundary. The signal-based recordPhase9Status path already exists and is replay-safe.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep adv_change_archive on bindTool and thread timeoutMs through bindTool
alternatives_considered.rationale: bindTool has no SafeExecuteOptions parameter and the registry guard test's extractRegistrationBlock only matches 'registerTool(' anchors. Threading options through bindTool would over-generalize a helper used by ~30 tools for one caller; the explicit registerTool block is the locality-correct, testable choice matching adv_gate_complete.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Implement all three coordinated edits: (1) tool-registry.ts:379-382 — replace bindTool with an explicit registerTool(...safeExecute(...,{ timeoutMs: 180_000 })) block carrying an rq-* rationale comment; add a matching guard test in tool-registry.test.ts:458-538 asserting timeoutMs >= ~180_000 and the rq citation. (2) change.ts:~2692 — call recordPhase9Status with a non-terminal status ('in_progress' or 'started', startedAt=now) immediately before the finalizeRelease/verify await, so a subsequent timeout/interruption leaves durable, retry-visible evidence consumed by the existing rq-archiveOrdering01 / reconcileArchivedBundleRetry recovery. (3) types/changes.ts:782 — widen Phase9FinalizationStatusSchema.status enum with the new member (replay-safe per workflows.ts:1481 opaque assignment); run pnpm run schemas:generate + keep schemas:check green if the schema is published.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Ship the coordinated fix. Deterministic verification cases the implementation agent can assert: (V1) tool-registry.test.ts — extractRegistrationBlock('adv_change_archive') is non-null (proves conversion to registerTool) AND matches /timeoutMs:\s*(\d[\d_]*)/ with value >= 180_000 AND contains the rq-* citation. (V2) change.archive-phase9.test.ts — a successful archive fires a non-terminal phase9_status ('in_progress'/'started') payload BEFORE the finalizeRelease mock resolves (assert ordering in mocks.workflow.signalPayloads or via mock call sequence), then a terminal 'done'. (V3) simulate outer-timeout: with the pre-finalization checkpoint in place, assert that after a rejected/aborted finalization the durable phase9_status is a recoverable non-'done' state and store.changes.save was NOT called (no archived transition) — mirrors the existing L636-669 failed-path test. (V4) bundle-present retry: with existing bundle + non-'done' phase9_status, adv_change_archive reconciles via reconcileArchivedBundleRetry / rq-archiveOrdering01 synthetic path without re-running finalization (assert finalizeRelease NOT re-invoked). (V5) schemas:check stays green after enum widening.
follow_ups: Confirm the exact non-terminal enum member name with the implementation agent ('in_progress' vs 'started'); either is replay-safe but the choice must be consistent across schema, change.ts checkpoint, and any gate.ts/archive-gate.ts status!=done predicates (change.ts:2858-2861, archive-gate.ts:399-401 already treat any non-'done' as incomplete, so both work).
Verify no chat-history-based reasoning was used: this report is sourced entirely from live file:line reads; the SESSION_HEALTH banner flagged history may be unsafe.

subagent_reports.topic: Design validation: archive terminal projection wedge — root-cause hypotheses and architecture

sources.label: disk get bundle-blind
sources.summary: get resolves only paths.changes, returns literal 'Change not found' at :348, no archive fallback (H1 confirmed).

sources.label: disk list bundle-aware
sources.summary: loadArchivedChanges reads paths.archive; merged when includeArchived — the get/list asymmetry.

sources.label: temporal get bundle-dominant
sources.summary: loadArchiveBundleDominantProjection forces status archived when hasArchiveBundle (claim 2 confirmed).

sources.label: target_path legacy routing
sources.summary: snapshot-ok and scaffold route to createLegacyStore; exact wedge surface (claim 3 confirmed).

sources.label: archive no timeout override
sources.summary: archive uses plain bindTool → inherits DEFAULT_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS=10000; checkpoint 35s / worker-restart 15s override (claim 4 confirmed).

sources.label: audited recovery writer
sources.summary: saveRecoveredChangeStatus asserts authorization then disk-direct saveChange, bypassing archiveChangeSignal (claim 5 confirmed).

sources.label: canonical-id dedupe helper
sources.summary: hasArchiveBundle handles non-eponymous archive dirs; reuse for rq-terminalProjectionTruth01.2 dedupe.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: All five root-cause claims confirmed at file:line. The wedge is primarily H1: target_path/snapshot-ok reads route to the legacy disk store whose get is bundle-blind, so a bundle-present change returns 'Change not found' while the native temporal get would surface it archived. Making the legacy disk get bundle-aware (read-only, mirroring loadArchiveBundleDominantProjection, deduped via hasArchiveBundle) is the correct minimal self-heal fix and does not touch write-side ordering. The adv_archive_repair reconcile mode is structurally identical to the shipped adv_change_status_repair audited flip. The typed idempotent archive-timeout plus raised ceiling matches existing override and idempotent-retry precedent.

validation.notes: No spec conflict. Two non-blocking cautions: (1) disk get bundle path must dedupe by canonical change.json.id per rq-terminalProjectionTruth01.2 — reuse hasArchiveBundle, do not reimplement; (2) add a test asserting temporal re-spread of status archived over a now-archived disk get is an idempotent no-op.

tradeoffs: Read-side self-heal keeps write ordering (rq-archiveRetirement01) untouched but requires the disk get and temporal get to agree on bundle dominance.
Cluster reconcile must stay strictly gated to avoid force-archiving incomplete changes.

alternatives_considered.rationale: Does not reach the snapshot-ok disk path; the cross-project/target_path wedge stays.

alternatives_considered.option: Route target_path through the temporal store

alternatives_considered.rationale: Moves the cliff without classification; rq-terminalAggregateRead01 wants structural degradation, not an unclassified ToolExecutionTimeout.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Proceed. Make legacy disk get bundle-aware via hasArchiveBundle-based canonical-id dedupe; add adv_archive_repair reconcile gated on bundle+gates+merge; add archive timeoutMs override + typed in-progress result; add the double-application no-op test.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Proceed with the design. Reuse hasArchiveBundle for canonical-id dedupe; keep all status writes through saveRecoveredChangeStatus.
follow_ups: Add regression test that temporal re-spread of archived over an already-archived disk get is a no-op (caution 2).

documents.proposal:
# Fix archive terminal projection wedge

## Problem
When `adv_change_archive` is interrupted at its terminal step (worker death, or the 10s tool ceiling firing while phase-9 git work continues), the change can be left in a state ADV's live reads cannot resolve to `archived` — even though the archive bundle is written and git is finalized. Recovery tools then also fail to help.

## Discovery Findings

### Skills Considered
- No matching ADV skill for Temporal terminal-step durability. `adv-audit` (spec/impl drift) is tangential; not loaded. Reported gap; core domain is internal Temporal/archive plumbing, not skill-shaped.

### Extends
No durable research pack. Grounded in source recon (this session): `plugin/src/tools/change.ts`, `plugin/src/archive/archive.ts`, `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/index.ts`, `plugin/src/storage/store-disk.ts`, `plugin/src/tools/_recovery-writers.ts`, and `.adv/specs/advance-workflow/spec.json`. New finding vs proposal: the proposal's premise ("no loadable change record") is FALSE for this incident — the active record and bundle both exist on disk.

### Conflict Scan
- Recurring class: adv_status hygiene shows ~12 changes stuck at `release` (alignCoordinateProjects, deepScanTemporalWorkflowHot, optimizeAdapterSurfaces, updateEpicOpsGuidance, fixLoopLedgerRegressions, fixDirectArchiveMerge, fixEpicTerminalProjection, persistPostArchiveSubagent, ensureTargetWorkers, addEpicTimestamps, bounceDeployedWorkers, strengthenMinimaxProviderHint). Some may be the same shipped-but-stuck wedge.
- Prior archive-recovery changes (archived): validateReleaseRecovery, fixDirectArchiveMerge, fixEpicTerminalProjection, persistPostArchiveSubagent, fixPhase9PrDetection. This is a repeatedly-patched area.
- Agenda: `ag-jPEv5v1T` (adv-recovery: "Repair portZellijLauncher release gate projection") is a sibling projection-repair symptom. No agenda item duplicates this change.
- No active in-flight change found targeting archive terminal-projection durability.

### Current State (source-grounded)
- Archive finalization order (`tools/change.ts` runArchive): spec deltas → bundle write (`archive.ts:816` createArchive, `status:"archived"` baked) → in-repo mirror → phase-9 commit/merge/push → release-gate durable → `phase9StatusUpdatedSignal` (writes disk projection) → **status flip** (`change.status="archived"; store.changes.save`) → epic projection → **removeChangeDir (active source cleanup)** → issue close → branch delete. Bundle-first is intentional (`rq-archiveRetirement01`).
- Status flip is a **Temporal signal** (`archiveChangeSignal`), not a direct disk write (`store-temporal/changes.ts:312`). If the workflow is gone/poisoned it throws; only `recoveryMode:"poisoned_history"` writes disk via `saveRecoveredChangeStatus`.
- Bundle-dominant read path EXISTS: `loadTerminalProjection` → `loadArchiveBundleDominantProjection` forces `status:"archived"` when `hasArchiveBundle` is true (`store-temporal/index.ts:446-492`, `rq-terminalProjectionTruth01`). So a bundle-present change SHOULD read as archived on the Temporal store.
- **Read asymmetry** (`rq`-relevant gap): legacy disk `get` is bundle-blind (`store-disk.ts:333-353`, returns literal "Change not found"), while legacy `list` is bundle-aware (`loadArchivedChanges` `:123`). `target_path`/`dryRun` reads route to the legacy store (`target-project.ts:284-296`), so `adv_change_show`/`adv_change_status_repair` via target_path can miss a bundle-only change.
- `adv_change_archive` has NO `timeoutMs` override → inherits `DEFAULT_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000` (`safe-execute.ts:240`); phase-9 push (300s git budget) easily exceeds it; `raceWithTimeout` does not abort the underlying work, so the tool reports `ToolExecutionTimeout` while archive continues.
- Observed on-disk truth for the incident: external `paths.archive/2026-07-13-alignProviderEvalTargets/` present; external `changes/alignProviderEvalTargets.json` STILL present (removeChangeDir did not run); in-repo mirror present; git trunk has archive+merge commits; remote branch deleted. All live reads via target_path returned "Change not found".

### Edge Cases
1. Worker dies between bundle write (step 2) and status flip (step 8): bundle + active record both remain; status never flips.
2. Tool ceiling fires mid-phase-9: tool returns ToolExecutionTimeout but archive keeps running; agent can't tell what completed.
3. target_path/dryRun recovery routes to bundle-blind legacy `get` → false "not found" even when bundle exists.
4. Bundle in external `paths.archive` vs in-repo `.adv/archive` mirror: a reader scanning the wrong root won't find it.

### Open Design Questions
1. **Why did the Temporal bundle-dominant read still return "not found" for this change?** Both active record and bundle exist on disk, yet reads failed. Trust: agent-only (runtime tracing). Blast radius: determines whether the fix is in the read path, the target_path routing, or the archive terminal step. Alternatives: (a) target_path forced legacy bundle-blind get; (b) deadline exhaustion in `loadArchiveProjection`; (c) canonical-id vs date-dir-name dedup miss. Must be traced in design.
2. **Scope breadth**: fix only the archive terminal-step durability + a bundle-anchored recovery tool, OR also reconcile the ~12 stuck-at-release changes as part of validating the fix? User-facing scope decision.
3. **Recovery entry point**: extend `adv_change_status_repair` to be bundle-anchored (work without a loadable workflow record), add a new `adv_archive_repair` reconcile mode, or make legacy `get` bundle-aware. Trust: joint. Blast radius: recovery ergonomics + read consistency.

### Draft Spec Deltas
Likely amend/extend existing archive-recovery requirements rather than net-new: `rq-archiveRecoveryConsistency01` (read-after-write), `rq-terminalProjectionTruth01` (bundle dominance), `rq-terminalAggregateRead01` (no bare ToolExecutionTimeout for terminal reads). Exact `rq-*` IDs to be firmed in design after the mechanism trace. G/W/T example: Given a change whose bundle exists and whose status flip signal was lost, When any ADV read resolves it, Then it reports `archived` (read-after-write parity across show/list/reflect).

### Related Pattern Scan
Same-class code: `saveRecoveredChangeStatus` (`_recovery-writers.ts:178`), `adv_change_status_repair` (`change.ts:3924`), `adv_archive_repair` (`change.ts:3153`), `loadArchiveBundleDominantProjection` (`index.ts:446`). Prior recovery specs `rq-releaseRepairRecovery01`, `rq-archiveOrdering01`. This is a well-trodden recovery surface with an unclosed gap.

### Completeness Verification
- Problem-completeness: MEDIUM confidence. The trigger (terminal-step interruption + tool ceiling) is well-characterized, but the precise reason live reads fail despite bundle+record on disk is UNVERIFIED and must be traced in design. The recurring stuck-at-release cluster suggests the problem is broader than one call.
- Solution-scope: MEDIUM. Three candidate fix surfaces (archive terminal step, recovery tool, read/routing asymmetry) — likely all three, to be confirmed after the mechanism trace.
- Reproduction finding classification: core symptom ("archive completes but change unreachable/unrepairable to archived") = `broken_capability` (may seed criteria). Sub-claim from the original proposal ("recovery fails because no loadable record exists") = `unverified` (record exists on disk) → downgraded to an out-of-scope note, NOT a criterion.
- Secondary surfaces: the ~12 stuck-at-release changes = unresolved user-facing scope question (surface in agreement). Sub-agent report-transport WorkflowNotFoundError = related but separate (out of scope unless design proves shared root cause).

### LBP Check
Internal Temporal/durability fix; no external solution applies. LBP: the shipped invariant should be reconstructable from durable on-disk evidence (bundle + gates + git), independent of live workflow health — ADV already leans this way (`loadArchiveBundleDominantProjection`); the fix should close the remaining gaps rather than invent a new mechanism.

### AMBIGUITY ANALYSIS
No blocking ambiguity in the confirmed problem. One HIGH advisory: the exact failure mechanism is unverified (open design question 1) — this is design-investigation work, not a proposal-scope ambiguity block. Coverage: B:C F:C S:P M:C.

### Recommended Objectives
1. An archive interrupted at the terminal step leaves the change reachable and repairable to `archived` through ADV tools, from durable on-disk evidence.
2. A single audited recovery tool reconciles a bundle-present change to a consistent `archived` projection even when the normal signal path failed and no healthy workflow exists.
3. `adv_change_archive` no longer reports a bare `ToolExecutionTimeout` that hides completed terminal work.
4. Regression test simulating terminal-step interruption after bundle write, proving read-after-write parity across show/list/reflect.
documents.problemStatement:
`adv_change_archive phase9:"run"` can exceed the default 10-second `safeExecute` tool budget while executing cumulative archive bundle/spec writes, git finalization, and Temporal signals. The outer timeout rejects the handler before `change.ts` can execute its local failure catch and record `phase9_status: "failed"`.

Observed impact in GitHub issue #216:
- Archive bundle and/or disk projection may be written before finalization completes.
- Release gate and terminal Temporal status may remain pending, missing, or unreachable.
- `phase9_status` may be absent, so operators receive only `ToolExecutionTimeout` rather than durable recovery evidence.
- Retry can re-run finalization against a bundle-present partial state without knowing which durable steps completed.

This overlaps directly with the existing terminal-projection wedge: a terminal-step timeout or worker loss can leave ADV without a reliably visible archived change, blocking reflection, cleanup, and audited recovery.

Required outcome: archive interruption must converge on a durable shipped, failed, or explicitly recoverable state. A Phase 9 operation that legitimately exceeds the historical 10-second safety net must use an explicit, tested timeout override; its status must be checkpointed before and after finalization; and bundle-present retries must reconcile safely rather than create another split-brain state.

# Design

## Root-Cause Hypotheses (validator-confirmed)
Independent validation confirmed all five source claims at file:line. The wedge is primarily **H1**: `target_path`/`snapshot-ok` reads route to the legacy disk store (`target-project.ts:284-307`) whose `get` is bundle-BLIND (`store-disk.ts:333-353`, literal `Change not found` at :348), while the native temporal `get` IS bundle-aware (`loadArchiveBundleDominantProjection`, `store-temporal/index.ts:460-489`). So a bundle-present change returns "Change not found" via target_path even though the bundle exists. **H2** (residual flat `changes/<id>.json` not resolving via the subdir-shaped legacy `get`) is a compounding possibility to disambiguate with the RED test; the fix covers both.

## Key Decisions
1. **Close the get/list bundle-awareness asymmetry (SC1/AC1).** Make the legacy disk `get` bundle-aware: when `paths.changes` has no record, consult the archive bundle and return the archived projection (`status:"archived"`). Read-only — cannot resurrect the active record (rq-archiveRetirement01.2). Sanctioned by rq-terminalProjectionTruth01 and rq-archiveRetirement01.2 ("archived lookups resolve from durable archived state OR the archive bundle").
2. **Audited bundle-anchored reconcile (SC2/AC2/AC3).** With #1, `adv_change_status_repair`'s `get` resolves bundle-present changes. Add an `adv_archive_repair` reconcile mode enumerating release-stuck changes, repairing only those satisfying the shipped invariant (durable bundle + all gates done + branch merged), leaving not-yet-archived changes untouched with per-change disposition reporting. Structurally identical to the shipped `adv_change_status_repair` audited flip. All status writes via `saveRecoveredChangeStatus` (AC6/DONT3).
3. **Typed idempotent archive timeout (SC3/AC4).** Give `adv_change_archive` a `timeoutMs` override (heavy-tool tier, cf. checkpoint 35s / worker-restart 15s in `tool-registry.ts`) and return a typed `finalizing`/`reconcile` result on the terminal-step path (aligns rq-terminalAggregateRead01: structural degradation, not a bare `ToolExecutionTimeout`). Preserve idempotent re-run (rq-archiveOrdering01).
4. **Preserve bundle-first ordering (C1).** Fix strengthens read/recovery only; write order unchanged.

## Implementation Strategy
1. RED: write an archive bundle + leave status unflipped (simulate lost terminal signal); assert `get`/`list(status:archived)`/reflect-eligibility report archived on BOTH stores and via target_path. Confirm current legacy `get` fails (H1) and characterize the flat-file case (H2).
2. Make legacy disk `get` bundle-aware. **Reuse `hasArchiveBundle` (`json.ts:918-933`) for canonical `change.json.id` dedupe (rq-terminalProjectionTruth01.2) — do NOT reimplement the non-eponymous-dir scan** (validator caution 1).
3. Confirm `adv_change_status_repair` now resolves bundle-present changes; keep its bundle+gates invariant refusal for incomplete changes.
4. Add `adv_archive_repair` reconcile mode for the release-stuck cluster (repair-only, refuse-incomplete, report dispositions).
5. Add `adv_change_archive` `timeoutMs` override + typed terminal-step in-progress/reconcile result.
6. GREEN + regression: read-after-write parity across show/list/reflect (AC5); required-field/incomplete-change refusals; idempotent re-run. **Add a test asserting the temporal re-spread of `status:"archived"` over a now-archived disk `get` is an idempotent no-op** (validator caution 2), so a future temporal refactor cannot assume a raw-active disk `get`.

## Affected Components (anticipated)
- `plugin/src/storage/store-disk.ts` (bundle-aware `get`)
- `plugin/src/storage/json.ts` (reuse `hasArchiveBundle` / `findArchiveBundle`)
- `plugin/src/tools/change.ts` (`adv_change_status_repair`, `adv_archive_repair` reconcile mode, `adv_change_archive` typed result)
- `plugin/src/tool-registry.ts` (archive `timeoutMs` override)
- `plugin/src/tools/_recovery-writers.ts` (audited writer reuse)
- Tests: `store-disk`, `change.status-repair`, `store-temporal/index.status-repair-readback`, archive terminal-step simulation.

## Spec Deltas (to firm in prep)
Extend existing requirements: rq-terminalProjectionTruth01 (bundle dominance now also enforced in legacy `get`), rq-archiveRecoveryConsistency01.3 (read-after-write parity across stores/routing), rq-terminalAggregateRead01 (no bare `ToolExecutionTimeout` hiding completed terminal work). Exact `rq-*` IDs + G/W/T finalized in prep.

## Risks / Mitigations
- Over-reach in cluster reconcile → strict bundle+gates+merge gate; report dispositions; never force-archive incomplete (C3/DONT2).
- Masking real failures → typed in-progress only after durable bundle write; else surface the real error (DONT2).
- Active fast-path regression → `get` is single-id resolve, not the active-list primitive; list bundle-merge stays gated on `includeArchived` (rq-activeListFastPath01 intact).
- Audit discipline → all status writes via `saveRecoveredChangeStatus` (rq-archiveRecoveryConsistency01.4).

## Independent Validation
adv-researcher: **PASS** (high confidence, low risk). All 5 root-cause claims confirmed at file:line; all 3 design decisions spec-consistent (rq-archiveRetirement01/.2, rq-terminalProjectionTruth01/.2, rq-activeListFastPath01, rq-archiveRecoveryConsistency01.2/.4, rq-archiveOrdering01.1, rq-terminalAggregateRead01). Rejected alternatives: temporal-only fix (misses snapshot-ok path), routing target_path through temporal (violates rq-targetReadAuthority01.2), bare ceiling raise (no classification). Two non-blocking cautions folded into Implementation Strategy steps 2 and 6. Report transport failed (WorkflowNotFoundError — the fragility under repair); orchestrator persisted the source-backed report.

## Design Leverage Scout
Skipped — internal durability/recovery fix reusing existing bundle-dominant read + audited recovery-writer primitives; leverage is consolidating the bundle-lookup via `hasArchiveBundle`.

# Executive Summary

## Outcome
Archive completion now remains recoverable when the durable archive bundle exists but its final status projection is interrupted. Approval accepts a bounded durability repair: archived reads self-heal, timeout responses explain safe reconciliation, and a controlled cluster reconcile repairs only already-shipped changes.

## Why It Matters
A completed archive no longer appears missing or in-flight solely because its terminal workflow signal was lost. Operators receive a typed, audited recovery path instead of an opaque timeout or a manual state-file workaround.

## Verdict
APPROVED

## What Was Built
1. Bundle-dominant legacy reads resolve durable archived state without recreating an active record (tk-23fd806e1cd9).
2. `adv_change_archive` reports a typed `still_finalizing` result after a post-bundle timeout and supports idempotent re-run reconciliation (tk-08b5f7e5c1fe).
3. Status repair recognizes bundle-dominant terminal state without a healthy workflow (tk-f7248412becc).
4. `adv_archive_repair action:"reconcile"` requires explicit approval, evidence, and reason; it repairs only bundle-present, fully-gated, merged candidates and reports all skipped dispositions (tk-29dd9803ee8a).

## What Was Verified
- Verdict: APPROVED; 0 blockers, 0 issues, 0 suggestions, 0 nits.
- Tests: independent focused suite passed 194 tests; smoke passed 62 tests; hardening focused suite passed 157 tests; `pnpm run check` and production build passed.
- Preview URL: not_applicable. This is an internal TypeScript plugin durability/recovery change with no browser-visible surface or visual-output task.
- Contract matrix: 19 required rows passed, respected, or marked approved out-of-scope; 0 failed, violated, or unknown.

## Remaining Concerns
- Non-blocking: the 420-second outer archive timeout is covered by deterministic tests, not a live-duration integration run.
- Live release-stuck cluster reconciliation remains an explicit post-deploy operator action and is not performed by this change.

## Supporting Evidence
- Checkpoints: tk-23fd806e1cd9, tk-08b5f7e5c1fe, tk-f7248412becc, tk-29dd9803ee8a, tk-a98c3ce70ad3.
- Review: `review:acceptance` READY; `harden:release` READY; independent verification `verifier:archive-terminal-projection` PASS.
- Contract review matrix: 19 rows persisted for this change.

## Consequence Context
1. Delivered value — complete archive bundles now remain visible and safely recoverable after terminal projection interruption (task checkpoints and contract matrix).
2. Enabling-only/follow-up dependency — no blocking dependency; optional live cluster reconcile follows deployment (planning evidence).
3. Ops readiness — hardening READY; reconcile remains operator-explicit and audited.
4. Migration/data impact — n/a; no application data migration or backfill (plugin recovery-state projection only).
5. Frontend/preview impact — not_applicable; no frontend or browser-visible output changed.
6. Collision/release risk — low; recovery paths are fail-closed on missing bundle, gates, merge proof, unreadable state, or probe failure (review and tests).
7. Open follow-ups — non-blocking live reconcile validation after deployment.
8. Next action — archive sign-off initiates Phase 9 release finalization.

## Release Readiness Summary
Harden review is READY: 157 focused tests, `pnpm run check`, production build, clean worktree/diff, and `git fsck` passed. No unresolved acceptance, design, release-safety, documentation, or cleanup blocker. Residual risk is limited to no live-duration exercise of the 420-second timeout; production reconcile remains explicit and audited.
